why: Plain preorder (root, left, right) on a binary tree; the only twist is that the tree is stored heap-style in an array, so the children of index i are 2i+1 and 2i+2 instead of pointers.
hints: In this array format, how do you get from a node to its children, and how do you know a child is missing?
Children of i are 2i+1 and 2i+2; a child is missing if its index is past the end or holds -1. Preorder visits the node, then the whole left subtree, then the right.
Use an explicit stack: pop i, output tree[i], push the right child then the left child (so left is processed first). O(n) time and space, no recursion-depth risk.
pitfalls: An empty array or a root of -1 means an empty tree: return [].
Check the index bound before reading tree[2i+1] or tree[2i+2].
Push right before left on the stack, or you get root-right-left order.
